name: Martian Hill Sphere
story: The outer limit of Mars's gravitational authority — about 1.08 million kilometres from the planet's centre. Inside this sphere, Mars's gravity wins over the Sun's; outside, the Sun reclaims anything you leave behind. Mars's Hill sphere is smaller than Earth's (1.5 M km) because Mars has less mass, even though Mars sits farther from the Sun. Both Martian moons orbit deep inside (Deimos at 2% of the Hill radius). No spacecraft has been placed near the boundary.
comparison: Roughly the distance from Earth to the Earth-Moon L2 Lagrange point. Anything captured into a Mars-bound trajectory has to dump enough energy to stay inside this boundary, or the Sun will pull it back into solar orbit.
